hero.title: About Vigia
hero.description: Flood alerts, risk maps and community preparedness built for Mozambique.

mission.title: Our Mission
mission.paragraph1: Vigia was created with a clear goal: helping Mozambican communities prepare for, respond to and recover from floods and cyclones. Mozambique sits downstream of several international river basins (Limpopo, Zambezi, Incomati, Pungwe, Buzi and others), and events like Cyclone Idai (2019) and Freddy (2023) showed the cost of not having information in time.
mission.paragraph2: The platform combines open weather and hydrological data, shelter and route maps, and training content in Portuguese, so residents, community leaders and volunteers know what to do before, during and after a flood.

safetyFirst.title: Safety First
safetyFirst.text: We prioritize the safety and well-being of communities above all else, ensuring our technology and training programs meet the highest standards.

excellence.title: Excellence
excellence.text: We strive for excellence in everything we do, from the accuracy of our alert systems to the quality of our training programs.

communityFocused.title: Community Focused
communityFocused.text: We design our solutions with real people in mind, creating tools that are accessible and effective for everyone in the community.

timeliness.title: Timeliness
timeliness.text: In emergency situations, every second counts. Our systems are designed to provide the fastest possible alerts and response guidance.

localFocus.title: Focused on Mozambique
localFocus.text: Designed for the Mozambican context: shared river basins, a rainy season from October to April, cyclones in the Mozambique Channel and communities with limited connectivity.

dataDriven.title: Data-Driven
dataDriven.text: We use advanced data analysis and AI to continuously improve our prediction models and emergency response recommendations.

founder.description: Mozambican developer who designed and builds Vigia end to end — from design to code — to put useful technology to work for disaster prevention in Mozambique.

flashFlood.title: Flash Flood Evacuation
flashFlood.description: Learn the correct steps to evacuate during a flash flood.

1.question: You receive a flash flood warning for your area. What should you do first?

options.1: Go outside to check the water level
options.2: Gather emergency supplies and important documents
options.3: Wait to see if water reaches your door
options.4: Turn on the TV and relax

1.explanation: Immediately gather emergency supplies (water, first-aid kit, flashlight) and important documents (ID, insurance). Time is critical in flash floods.

2.question: Your area is flooding. Which is the safest evacuation route?

options.1: Drive through a road with flowing water
options.3: Move to higher ground using roads away from water
options.4: Go to the basement for shelter

2.explanation: Always move to higher ground. Never drive through floodwater (6 inches can knock you down, 2 feet can float a car). Never go to basements during floods.

3.question: You encounter a flooded road. What should you do?

options.2: Turn around, don't drown - find an alternate route
options.3: Wait for the water to recede

3.explanation: Turn around, don't drown. Just 12 inches of moving water can carry away a small car. Always find an alternate route to higher ground.

4.question: You reach a safe shelter. What should you do first?

options.1: Go back to check on your house
options.2: Register at the shelter and inform family you're safe
options.3: Leave immediately to find a better place

4.explanation: Register at the shelter so rescue services know you're safe. Contact family members. Follow shelter staff instructions and stay until authorities say it's safe to leave.

emergencyShelter.title: Emergency Shelter
emergencyShelter.description: Learn how to set up and manage an emergency shelter.

1.question: What is the most important item to have in an emergency kit?

options.2: Clean drinking water (1 gallon per person per day)
options.4: A deck of cards for entertainment

1.explanation: Clean water is the #1 survival priority. Store at least 3 days of water (1 gallon per person per day). You can survive weeks without food, but only 3 days without water.

2.question: How should you prepare your home before a flood arrives?

options.1: Open all windows to let water flow through
options.2: Move valuables to upper floors and seal lower openings
options.4: Turn on all electronics to keep them charged

2.explanation: Move important items and electronics to upper floors. Use sandbags or barriers at doors. Turn off electricity at the breaker if flooding is imminent.

3.question: After the flood, when is it safe to return home?

options.1: As soon as the water recedes from the street
options.2: When local authorities officially declare it safe

3.explanation: Only return when authorities declare it safe. Floodwater can hide dangers (contamination, structural damage, downed power lines). Always have the building inspected first.

4.question: You find standing water in your home after a flood. What is the main danger?
4.explanation: Floodwater is often contaminated with sewage, chemicals, and debris. Electrical systems submerged in water create electrocution risk. Never touch electrical equipment in standing water.
